I will also print the actual output for debugging purposes.","tool":"run_test","args":{"source":"import pytest
from rich.console import Console


def test_soft_wrap_background_color():
    console = Console()
    
    # Capture the output of the first print with soft_wrap=True
    from io import StringIO
    import sys
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is on", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=True)
    console.print("still has background color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue().splitlines()
    print(printed_output)  # Debugging line to see the actual output
    assert len(printed_output) > 1
    assert printed_output[0] == 'soft wrap is on'
    assert printed_output[1] == 'still has background color from previous line'
    assert '\x1b[48;5;255m' in output.getvalue()  # Check if background color is present
    
    # Capture the output of the second print with soft_wrap=False
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is off", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=False)
    console.print("correctly has no color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue().splitlines()
    assert len(printed_output) > 1
    assert printed_output[0] == 'soft wrap is off'
    assert printed_output[1] == 'correctly has no color from previous line'
    assert '\x1b[48;5;255m' not in output.getvalue()  # Check if no ANSI escape code is present"}}
